subject: Architecture
title: Lotte World Tower: Seoul's Giant
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lotte World Tower: Seoul's Giant.

hook.text: South Korea's tallest building took 13 years to approve because of fears it would crash into a nearby air base.

buildup.text: At 1,819 feet, Lotte World Tower tapers gently like a traditional Korean ceramic brush.

discovery.text: Its glass floor observation deck hangs 1,600 feet up — the highest glass-bottom floor in the world.

twist.text: The tower houses a concert hall, aquarium, hotel, offices, and apartments — a vertical city in one shaft.

climax.text: Seoul's skyline was once limited by airspace rules. Lotte proved supertalls could coexist with flight paths.

punchline.text: Thirteen years of 'no' turned into South Korea's tallest 'yes.'

quiz.question: Why did Lotte World Tower take 13 years to approve?
options: Environmental concerns about the Han River
Fears it would interfere with a nearby air base
Disagreements over the building's design style
